entries.notes: Brand name. No pronunciation is recorded anywhere in slot-books or the brand kit, so none is assumed. Preview the default reading, set an alias or IPA if it is wrong, then approve.
The website, read in calls to action. Check it is said as 'use Iker dot com', not 'oo-SEE-ker'. A likely alias is 'use Iker dot com' once the reading of Iker is settled.
Nigerian currency. Check the voice says NYE-rah, as Nigerians do.

Naira sign, as in ₦45,000 on screen. Kept here as a reminder rather than a rule: the term matcher ignores a term followed directly by a digit, so an alias would not apply to '₦45,000', and an alias could not move the word after the number anyway. Preview a sentence with an amount; if the voice skips the sign or says 'N', write the amount out in the narration ('45,000 naira').
A hundredth of a Naira. Rare in narration; check it is said KOH-boh.
Payment provider Iker uses for subscription billing. Check it is said as 'pay stack'.
Fallback payment provider for subscription billing. Check it is said as 'flutter wave'.
Iker's pilot city. Check it is said ah-BOO-jah.
Check it is said LAY-goss, as Nigerians do, not LAH-gohs.
Product term ('Add walk-in'). Check the stress falls on WALK.
Initialism, normally spelled out: C-S-V. Used for import and export.
Initialism, normally spelled out: P-D-F. Used for reports and statements.
Direct messages, spelled out: D-Ms ('dee-ems'). Used in 'Stop chasing payments in DMs'.
